attributes.readMe:
## Authorship Metadata (AM)

Who made this — the creative credit, not the legal owner. That split is the whole point of having two fields: `PublishingMetadataField` answers *who put it out and on what terms*, and a reader checking whether they may reuse something does not care who drew it.

### Shape

| Field | Why it is shaped this way |
|---|---|
| `creators` | **containsMany**, not a single `author`. Most real work has more than one hand on it, and one string forces the first person to stand for all of them. |
| `organization` | Separate from the people. A studio is not a co-author, and collapsing them loses the distinction a credit line needs. |
| `tool` | What produced the artifact — a slicer, a camera, a generator. Sits here because it answers "how was this made", and because a file whose only authorship fact is `Bambu Studio` still tells a reader something real. |
| `sourceUrl`, `createdOn`, `note` | Provenance detail. |

### `credit` — one line, always something

Computed. Falls through **creators → organization → tool**, so a credit slot can print it without knowing which facts were extractable. `hasCredit` is the absence signal.

### Why this is new rather than a rename

These facts are already captured, but **per family and under family names**: a 3D model stores `designer` on `model3d`, a Word document stores its author inside `DocumentInfoField`, an image carries EXIF. Nothing reads "who made this?" across families, because there is nowhere to read it from.

### The consolidation trap — read before using

**Adding this field on its own makes things worse, not better.** A document would then carry authorship in two places that can disagree.

This is only finished when the per-family facts are *projected into* it — the same way every 3D format projects onto one `Model3dMetadataField` instead of each carrying its own mesh counts. Until that projection exists, treat this as **the destination, not the source of truth**.

### Non-goals

Not a permissions model. Not a `Person` card — the creators are names, because the systems these facts come from store names, and forcing a card link would mean inventing a person record for every EXIF string.
